Specifically, you posed the following issued for our resolution, to wit: e. What is the status of the subject Ordinance? Is a private party justified in relying in the subject Ordinance (considering the provisions of-sec. 56 (d) of the Local Government Code)? What are the a-rounds for finding against a Municipal Ordinance by its Provincial level counterpart (considering the provisions of Sec. 56 (c) of the Local Government Code)?" In reply thereto, please be informed that this Department has already answered a similar query in DILG Opinion No. 52, series of 2007. In the said legal opinion, we opined that since an ordinance was already enacted by the Sangguniang Bayan, duly approved by the Municipal Mayor and has. undergone the procedural requirements for its effectivity, the same is considered valid unless declared invalid by the proper court. As such, any issue o question thereon as to its substantive validity and enforceability should be addressed by filing a special civil action for declaratory relief before the proper court in accordance with Section 1, Rules 63 of the Revised Rules of Court.
